page: OVHcloud b3-32-flex is a General Purpose cloud instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration lacks simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core) and supplies 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Bundled storage comprises a 50 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent computational throughput across varied workloads. The processor achieved a strong single-core stress-ng score of 3,067.48 (top 25%) and an average multi-core score of 24,497.8. In Geekbench testing, the instance logged 1,900.0 points in single-core and 9,708.0 in multi-core routines, marked by strong text processing throughput (2,629.0). Memory evaluations via PassMark yielded a strong result of 2,836.59, supported by an uncached read bandwidth of 127.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 54.63 GB/sec. Specialized tasks, including small-model LLM generation (283.15 tokens/sec), perform above median tiers.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance combined with dedicated physical cores delivers steady execution without resource contention, representing a cost-efficient deployment profile for general computational workloads. However, with only 50 GB of bundled local NVMe storage and absence of AVX-512 instruction support, data-heavy applications requiring large datasets or vectorized scientific computations may require external storage attachments or specialized compute nodes.

OVHcloud b3-32-flex is suited for general enterprise applications, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web application serving, software compilation pipelines, and light machine learning inference.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core stress-ng execution (3,067.48) and top-quartile PassMark memory performance (2,836.59), alongside consistent multi-core compute metrics across Geekbench and compression tasks. It is appropriately configured for production web serving, microservice clusters, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier databases.
